links.title: PolicyGuide: From Guarding One Action to Guiding the Whole Workflow for Policy-Compliant LLM Agents

evidence: Abstract and Table 1 (Section 4.2): PolicyGuide raises mean Pass^4 from 0.42 to 0.62 across airline/retail/telecom with GPT 5.4, largest gain on telecom (0.19 to 0.61); Table 1 reports per-domain Pass^1/Pass^4 vs ReAct, ToolGuard, and PolicyGuard.

Appendix C, Tables 12-13: pooled stratified McNemar tests favor PolicyGuide over ReAct (p<10^-8) and PolicyGuard (p<10^-12), but per-domain bootstrap CIs cross zero for Airline vs PolicyGuard (+0.040 [-0.080,+0.160]) and Retail vs ReAct (+0.018 [-0.070,+0.105]).

Section 4.7 and Table 5: author-designed Telecom trace rubric gives PolicyGuide 56.2% process-valid rate vs 17.5% (ReAct) and 13.1% (PolicyGuard); Limitations states it is exploratory with no second-annotator agreement estimate.

Section 4.6 and Figure 6: lowest CRAFT attack-success rate (0.087 per-trial vs 0.125 PolicyGuard, 0.200 ReAct) on 20 airline attack tasks only; Limitations notes the released Retail CRAFT set could not be reproduced and no official Telecom set exists.

Limitations section: retail overall gain over ReAct is not significant with only 10 PV tasks; verifier judgments are probabilistic and fail-open; deployed schedule does not satisfy Theorem 1's ideal-verifier assumptions (Corollary 2).
Appendix D, Tables 14-15: guide costs $0.34-0.56/task with 7.4-11.5 verifier calls and 5.45-5.78x wall-clock overhead vs ReAct.

Section 4.5 and Table 4: GPT 5.4-authored airline workflow transfers unchanged to Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Gemini 2.5 Pro agents; the paper states transfer across workflow-author models remains untested.

Appendices E, G, H and Ethics Statement: frozen workflows manually verified with programmatic validation (Table 16), load-bearing prompts reproduced verbatim, example graphs visualized, and a commitment to release prompts, schemas, and analysis artifacts for reproducibility.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Clearly in-scope LLM-agent methodology: an external workflow-graph verifier that guides policy compliance of tool-using agents, hitting high-weight preferences (Agents & Tool Use, LLMs, AI Safety, Red-Teaming/Evaluation). The synthesis of action-guard safeguards with workflow enforcement is a sensible but incremental contribution over the authors' own PolicyGuard and existing SOP/workflow-agent lines; the intervention-coverage theorem (Appendix A) is a useful formalization but assumes an ideal binding verifier the deployed advisory system does not satisfy, as the paper itself concedes. Evaluation is comparatively rigorous for the area: three tau2-bench domains, n=4, Pass^1/Pass^4, paired bootstrap and stratified McNemar tests (Appendix C), matched FlowAgent comparison, cross-agent transfer, CRAFT red-teaming, and detailed cost/wall-clock analysis (5.45-5.78x overhead, $0.34-0.56/task). Evidence is weakened by a single benchmark family, small task counts (airline 50, retail 10 PV), several domain-level CIs crossing zero (Airline vs PolicyGuard +0.040 [-0.080,+0.160]; Retail vs ReAct +0.018, non-significant per Limitations), and an author-designed trace rubric with no second-annotator agreement. CRAFT coverage is airline-only (20 tasks) with acknowledged non-reproducible retail sets. Generalizability is moderate: three agent families on airline only, single workflow author, transfer across authors untested. Reproducibility is good on paper (full prompts in Appendix G, algorithm, frozen-graph validation in Appendix E) but rests on a future release commitment rather than released artifacts.

primary_link.title: PolicyGuide: From Guarding One Action to Guiding the Whole Workflow for Policy-Compliant LLM Agents

papers.summary: Customer-service LLM agents must follow organizational policy when acting on a user's behalf. Compliance failures arise from either forbidden actions, such as granting an ineligible change, or omitted procedural requirements, such as identification or confirmation. Runtime safeguards can intervene on risky actions, but action-local checks do not guide an agent through a multi-step procedure. Workflow-following systems support prescribed process execution, but primarily target workflow completion
papers.summary_zh: 客服 LLM 代理需遵循組織政策行事,但現有防護多在單一動作層級攔截,無法引導多步驟流程;工作流程代理雖能執行既定程序,卻以流程完成而非防護行為為主要目標。本文提出 PolicyGuide,將每個領域政策編譯成工作流程圖,並在使用者輪次邊界啟動主動式驗證器:驗證器從持久化的圖狀態出發,核對所有未結案請求,沿合規路徑回傳逐步補救指引;未經授權的變更工具呼叫會被攔截並觸發修正檢查。在 τ²-bench 的航空、零售與電信領域,搭配 GPT 5.4 代理與驗證器,平均 Pass^4 從 0.42 提升至 0.62,其中流程結構最強的電信領域從 0.19 躍升至 0.61;同一工作流程可轉移至 Claude Sonnet 4.6 與 Gemini 2.5 Pro 代理。CRAFT 紅隊測試顯示其攻擊成功率最低(單次 0.087),作者自訂的電信軌跡審計也錄得最高流程合規率(56.2%)。消融實驗指出外部圖形追蹤是關鍵成分。此工作將政策合規從單一動作檢查擴展為涵蓋整體程序的持續引導。
papers.title: PolicyGuide: From Guarding One Action to Guiding the Whole Workflow for Policy-Compliant LLM Agents
papers.title_zh: PolicyGuide:從守護單一動作到引導完整工作流程的合規 LLM 代理

links.title: SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

evidence: Abstract: 'SAPO trains stably and outperforms PPO and GRPO by mean +15.1 and +12.1 percentage points, respectively, while eliminating the memory cost of a separate critic model and reducing per-iteration runtime by 33.2% over PPO. (Going On)'

Section 4.1: 'We reserve two existing vocabulary entries, w+ and w-, exclusively as a value basis... their relative evidence defines a normalized scalar readout' with V and Q read at pre-action and post-action causal boundaries.
Section 5.1: 'Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as the base models... learning rate of 1e-6, and a KL-penalty coefficient of 0.01... 4 NVIDIA H200s and 8 NVIDIA A40s.'
Table 1 caption: 'we report the mean and standard deviation over three random seeds... Most entries in this table are reported by Feng et al. [4]'

Section 5.3: 'SAPO reduces the total measured runtime from 451.2 s to 301.4 s, yielding a 33.2% reduction over PPO', with module-level breakdown (generation 306.4s to 221.4s; critic stages 61.4s eliminated).

Section 5 research questions include '(2) How sensitive is SAPO to its components...' and '(4) Can SAPO effectively maintain stable performance over continuous training iterations', but no ablation or stability results appear in the provided Sections 5.2-5.3.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core-topic paper on agentic RL for LLM agents (strong match to Agents & Tool Use, LLMs, RL, Training preferences). The central idea—reading V and Q from a two-token logit-difference value basis at distinct causal boundaries of one autoregressive backbone, removing both the separate critic and group-relative sampling—is a genuine and reasonably novel design point relative to Hydra-PPO/POISE/SAO described in Section 2. However, rigor is limited by an incomplete draft: the abstract ends with '(Going On)', and Section 5 poses ablation-sensitivity and training-stability research questions that are not answered in the provided Sections 5.2-5.3, which contain only main results and a runtime breakdown. Table 1 provides 3-seed mean±std results on ALFWorld/WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B, but notes 'Most entries in this table are reported by Feng et al. [4]', so several baselines are inherited rather than re-run. Only two text-agent benchmarks, no reasoning/code/math evaluation, limiting generalizability. Reproducibility is mixed: Section 5.1 gives lr, KL coefficient, turn limits, step count, and hardware, but key hyperparameters (reserved tokens w+/w-, tau_v, c_V, c_Q, clip epsilons, invalid-action penalty c_inv from Section 4) and code availability are not stated in the document.

primary_link.title: SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

papers.summary: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) has become a critical stage in the post-training of large language models. Existing critic-free, group-relative methods estimate policy advantages from multiple rollouts, avoiding the substantial memory overhead of conventional proximal policy optimization (PPO) and achieving strong performance on long-horizon interactive tasks. Despite their success, recent studies revealed three limitations: (1) Lack explicit value generalization and effective temporal credi
papers.summary_zh: 代理式強化學習已成為 LLM 後訓練的關鍵階段,但免 critic 的群組相對方法(如 GRPO)缺乏顯式價值泛化與時間性信用分配,在長程任務易出現優勢崩塌,且取樣預算與效能難以兼得。本文提出 SAPO,讓策略與價值函數共享單一自迴歸骨幹:利用 LLM 的自迴歸結構,在反應前後兩個因果邊界分別讀出狀態價值 V 與動作價值 Q(以兩個保留詞元的 logit 差實作),並以因果遮罩強制條件分離,同時獨立最佳化 PPO 目標與輔助的 on-policy SARSA 目標。為穩健估計每個輪次的貢獻,作者進一步結合 λ-returns 與批次正規化,構成軌跡層級的廣義優勢估計。在 ALFWorld 與 WebShop 上以 Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B 實驗,SAPO 相較 PPO 平均提升 15.1 個百分點、相較 GRPO 提升 12.1 個百分點,同時免除獨立 critic 模型的記憶體成本,單次迭代執行時間較 PPO 減少 33.2%。此結果顯示顯式價值學習不必依賴重複模型或昂貴的多重取樣,為長程代理式 RL 提供高效路徑。
papers.title: SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.title_zh: SAPO:代理式強化學習之單一 Rollout 自迴歸策略最佳化

links.title: Let's Scale Step by Step: Compute-Efficient Hyperparameter Transfer for Large-Scale Mixture-of-Experts

evidence: Abstract: proposes two-step hyperparameter transfer for large-scale MoE, extrapolating optimal learning rates to trillion-token horizons with R²=0.95 and validating on a 155B total / 17B active parameter model pretrained from scratch.

Section 3.2, Figure 3: under μP the optimal learning rate identified at the 0.6B/0.3B-active base proxy transfers to 2x, 4x, 8x width-scaled MLA MoE models (up to 30.7B total), while Standard Parameterization fails to transfer.

Appendix E, Table 4: retrospective held-out validation predicts unseen ~462B–502B token budgets with predicted/actual optimal-LR ratios of 1.033–1.058 (average discrepancy ≈4.4%) using only 255B–350B data points for fitting.

Section 5 (Conclusion): authors state exhaustive full-scale sweeps to definitively verify the optimality of the predicted 3.85e-4 learning rate are computationally infeasible, relying instead on stable loss (Figure 6) and benchmark scores (Figure 7).

Section 3.3.3, Figure 8: comparison to dots.llm1, GLM-4.5-Air, Hunyuan-A13B, DeepSeek-V4-Flash uses estimated 6ND compute with N as active parameters and all models evaluated with the authors' own evaluation harness.

Appendix A and Table 3: detailed configurations and hyperparameters are given (batch sizes 0.5M–32M tokens, weight decay 1e-1, z-loss 5e-6, EMA α=0.6, LR sweep grids), but training uses 'an internal fork of Megatron-LM' and internal corpora with no code or data availability claim.

Section 5: acknowledged limitations include restriction to MLA + Muon, inability to disentangle the sparsity axis from width scaling, and deferral of per-expert learning-rate adaptation to future work.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM pretraining methodology paper: compute-efficient hyperparameter (learning-rate) transfer for large-scale MoE via a two-step framework (μP width transfer + token-horizon scaling law), validated by pretraining a 155B/17B-active MoE on 10T tokens. Strongly matches LLM, scaling/efficiency, and training/optimization preferences; it is not a pure domain application. Novelty is moderate: it extends existing μP-MoE work (Małaśnicki et al.) and token-horizon LR scaling (Bjorck et al., step law) to MLA+Muon with coupled width-sparsity scaling; the EMA-based proxy-checkpoint trick is practical but incremental. Rigor is solid: SP-vs-μP and dense-vs-MoE controls, multi-scale proxies, quadratic LR fits, log-log regression, and a retrospective held-out validation (Table 4, ratios 1.033–1.058). However, the headline 10T-token prediction is ~20x beyond the fitted 255B–502B range and its optimality is only indirectly supported by stable loss and benchmark scores, as the authors candidly admit in the Conclusion. Evidence strength is limited by this lack of direct verification and by Figure 8 comparisons resting on estimated 6ND compute under their own eval harness. Generalizability is constrained to MLA+Muon with joint width-sparsity scaling; sparsity is not disentangled. Reproducibility is partial: Table 3 and Appendix A give configs and hyperparameters (EMA α=0.6, batch sizes, weight decay, z-loss), but training uses an internal corpus, an internal Megatron-LM fork, and no code/data release is stated.

primary_link.title: Let's Scale Step by Step: Compute-Efficient Hyperparameter Transfer for Large-Scale Mixture-of-Experts

papers.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures significantly expand model capacity without a proportional increase in computational cost. However, optimizing their hyperparameters---particularly the learning rate---at extreme scales of both model size and token budget via sweeping remains computationally prohibitive. In this paper, we propose a compute-efficient, two-step hyperparameter transfer framework that estimates optimal learning rates for training large MoE models by transferring them across sca
papers.summary_zh: 混合專家架構能以有限運算成本擴充模型容量,但在極大模型與 token 預算下,以全面搜尋找出最佳學習率並不可行。本文提出兩階段超參數遷移框架:第一步針對採用 Multi-head Latent Attention(MLA)與 Muon 最佳化器的 MoE 架構,制定 μP(Maximal Update Parameterization)調整,驗證最佳學習率可跨寬度縮放一致遷移(在標準參數化下則無法遷移);第二步建立 token 維度的預測縮放律,對小型 proxy 模型在有限預算下估計出的最佳學習率進行對數空間線性迴歸(R²=0.95),外推至 10 兆 token 的長程訓練,得到最佳學習率 3.85×10⁻⁴。方法上利用 WSD 排程器搭配權重指數移動平均(EMA),從單一訓練運行抽取多個檢查點,避免昂貴的衰減實驗。作者以此方法從零預訓練 155B 總參數、17B 活化參數的基礎模型達 10 兆 token,訓練損失全程穩定無尖峰,評測表現具競爭力,證明小型 proxy 實驗即可準確預測大規模訓練組態,大幅降低超參數搜尋的運算負擔。
papers.title: Let's Scale Step by Step: Compute-Efficient Hyperparameter Transfer for Large-Scale Mixture-of-Experts
papers.title_zh: Let's Scale Step by Step:大規模混合專家的高運算效率超參數遷移

links.title: Projecting BrowseComp-Plus onto ClimbMix: Toward More Realistic Corpora for Agentic Search

evidence: Abstract: 'evidence recall fall from 84.3% to 21.4% while issuing 63% more search calls' and strongest agent 80.7% vs 86.0% accuracy
Section 4 (Figure 2): pipeline reduces 830 questions to 326 answerable, 65 all-hops grounded, 57 after human verification
Section 5, 'Projection pipeline reproducibility': 'Projection, answerability, and qrel expansion are therefore agentic and not exactly reproducible'
Table 1: GPT–5.6 Sol recall 84.3%→21.4%, tool calls 60.2→98.3; Gemma 4 31B IT accuracy 26.3%→15.8% with 39/57 insufficient-evidence reports (Section 6 audit)
Table 2: GPT–5.6 Sol closed-book accuracy 70.2% on the 57 projected questions vs 46.1% on all 830, an acknowledged memorization confound (Section 6, 'How much is already memorized?')
Section 4 Stage 4 / Figure 7(a): 347 question–hop pairs, ~a quarter draw on >40 documents, so union Recall/nDCG are 'dominated by the most redundant hops'
Released artifacts section: Hugging Face castorini/cmass and GitHub pipeline, prompts in Appendix B; 'Two items are deliberately absent' (hop decompositions, per-hop qrels)
Section 2 and 3: corpus selection justified by ClimbMix scale (400B tokens, 553M docs, 559 GB Lucene index) and independence from any benchmark
llm_evaluation.rationale: Highly relevant to agentic search, retrieval evaluation, and LLM agents (high-weight preferences: Agents & Tool Use, LLMs, RAG, Evaluation). Core contribution—inverting benchmark projection so questions survive only if every reasoning hop is already grounded in a large natural corpus—is a fresh twist on old cross-corpus projection, though concurrent BrowseComp-Wikipedia narrows the gap. Rigor is solid in verification structure (auto + independent agent + human) but undermined by a tiny final set (57 questions; the 86.0→80.7 accuracy drop is ~3 questions with no significance testing), author-only human review, unvalidated LLM judges, BM25-only retrieval, and construction/evaluation sharing one retrieval stack. Evidence reporting is detailed and unusually honest (closed-book 70.2% memorization confound, Gemma give-up audit), yet small-n headline claims and the self-acknowledged fact that recall over union qrels is dominated by redundant hops weaken the benchmark's immediate utility. Generalizability is claimed but demonstrated on exactly one benchmark/corpus pair with ~7% yield. Reproducibility is good (artifacts, prompts, per-stage scripts released) but the paper itself concedes the agentic projection stages are 'not exactly reproducible' and depend on proprietary models.

primary_link.title: Projecting BrowseComp-Plus onto ClimbMix: Toward More Realistic Corpora for Agentic Search

papers.summary: The BrowseComp-Plus benchmark disentangled the evaluation of agentic search by replacing opaque web search with a fixed corpus, so that an agent's role can be separated from the retriever's. That corpus, however, holds only about 100K documents and was assembled from the supporting documents of the benchmark's own queries plus mined hard negatives, so the evidence and the distractors were both selected per query. We introduce $\text{BrowseComp-Plus}_{\text{CM}}$, which keeps the BrowseComp-Plus
papers.summary_zh: BrowseComp-Plus 以固定語料庫將代理與檢索器的評測解耦,但其約 10 萬份文件皆由查詢的支持文件與挖掘出的困難負例組成,證據與干擾項皆為查詢量身挑選,不夠自然。本文提出投影管線,保留原始問題但將證據轉移至 NVIDIA 釋出的 ClimbMix——一個 4000 億 token、5.53 億文件、與任何基準無關的預訓練語料。管線將每題分解為原子推理步驟,在語料庫中為每一步尋找證據,僅當自動驗證、獨立代理與人工審查皆確認每步獲得支持時才保留問題。830 題測試問題僅 57 題存活,形成具問題層級相關性判斷的 BrowseComp-Plus_CM。投影後難度轉移到檢索端:最強代理 GPT-5.6 Sol 的答案正確率僅從 86.0% 降至 80.7%,證據召回率卻從 84.3% 驟降至 21.4%,且需多打 63% 的搜尋呼叫;較弱代理的召回率更跌破 3%。此基準證明在天然大規模語料上,檢索而非推理才是主要瓶頸,為代理式搜尋研究提供更真實的測試環境。
papers.title: Projecting BrowseComp-Plus onto ClimbMix: Toward More Realistic Corpora for Agentic Search
papers.title_zh: 將 BrowseComp-Plus 投影至 ClimbMix:邁向更貼近現實的代理式搜尋語料

links.title: OenoBench: A Wine-Domain Benchmark for Knowledge-Grounded Evaluation of Large Language Models

evidence: Abstract: 3,266 MCQs across six pillars and four difficulty tiers built from 38,104 atomic provenance-tagged facts; 16 frontier configs evaluated, o3 leads at 83.6%.
Section 4.2 / Table 5: agent B2 ClosedBookSolvability shows κ≈0.007 vs human gold sheet (humans solve ~12% vs LLM panel ~83%); questions retained with disclosure.
Section 5.3 / Table 9: per-config Self-Preference Scores with 95% bootstrap CIs; Anthropic configs +9 to +10 pp, Google configs −6 to −10 pp, OpenAI statistically zero.
Section 5.5 / Table 11: closed-book minus contextual gap mean +32.6 pp, significant at L2–L4 tiers (+31.8/+25.1/+26.4 pp, CIs exclude zero).
Section 7: explicit limitations — snapshot corpus dated 2026-04-01, B2 calibration failure, residual Anthropic self-preference not fully neutralised.
Appendix B.1: 19 of 35 original scrapers contained hard-coded LLM-generated facts disguised as scraped data and were rebuilt against live sources.
Appendix E.1/E.4/E.6: dataset released CC-BY-SA-4.0 on HuggingFace, code Apache 2.0 on GitHub with reproducibility scripts, $783 total API spend itemised, 771/771 unit tests passing.
Appendix C Tables 8–14: reasoning lift only significant for DeepSeek R1 vs V3 (+6.8 pp), with per-tier and per-domain breakdowns supporting the headline claims.
llm_evaluation.rationale: In-scope LLM evaluation paper: constructs a knowledge-grounded multiple-choice benchmark and evaluates 16 frontier LLM configurations, with methodology centered on LLM-as-judge calibration, contamination control, and self-preference bias rather than on the niche wine domain itself, so it is not a pure domain application. Novelty is moderate: the scrape-to-audit recipe assembles known ideas (multi-model generation, tiered provenance, LLM audits, κ-calibration from LegalBench/FinanceBench lineage), but the finding that LLM judges over-report closed-book solvability (κ≈0.007 vs humans) and the family-asymmetric self-preference results are genuinely interesting. Rigor is above average: human gold-sheet calibration, 95% bootstrap CIs throughout, per-domain/strategy/difficulty ablations, post-eval defect removal, and candid limitations (residual Anthropic +9pp SPS, B2 miscalibration, snapshot corpus); caveats include a 50-question gold sheet with the lead author as a rater and C4 difficulty relabeling relying on Gemini self-rating. Evidence is strong with detailed tables, cost telemetry, and 771/771 unit tests, though several attributions (e.g., Google's negative SPS as 'harder-by-phrasing') are interpretive. Generalizability is limited by the single-domain snapshot, despite the plausible domain-agnostic pipeline claim. Reproducibility is excellent: CC-BY-SA-4.0 dataset, Apache-2.0 code, process log, and scripts.

primary_link.title: OenoBench: A Wine-Domain Benchmark for Knowledge-Grounded Evaluation of Large Language Models

papers.summary: We introduce OenoBench, a wine-domain knowledge benchmark of 3,266 multiple-choice questions across six pillars (regions, grape varieties, viticulture, winemaking, producers, business) and four difficulty tiers. The corpus is built from 38,104 atomic, source-anchored facts extracted by 35 provenance-verified scrapers from government registries (INAO, TTB, OIV), peer-reviewed journals, and Wikipedia/Wikidata. Our methodological contribution is an LLM-driven pipeline in which language models refor
papers.summary_zh: 主流知識基準如 MMLU、GPQA 廣而不深,題目也常疑遭訓練資料汙染。本文提出 OenoBench,首個葡萄酒領域的知識評測基準:3,266 道選擇題橫跨產區、葡萄品種、葡萄栽培、釀造、生產者與商業六大支柱及四個難度層級,語料由 35 個經來源驗證的爬蟲從 INAO、OIV、TTB、期刊與 Wikipedia 等提取的 38,104 條原子事實構成。方法論核心是 LLM 驅動的管線:語言模型僅負責重寫與審計,絕不作為事實來源,每題皆可追溯至 URL。題目由五種策略、五個生成器模型產生,再經九個自動審計代理(以 Cohen's κ 對照人類黃金標準校準)把關,並揭露 LLM 評審會高估閉卷可解性。評測 16 個前沿組態顯示:整體正確率介於 53%–84%,o3 以 83.6% 居首;推理模式增益僅 DeepSeek R1(+6.8 個百分點)顯著;Anthropic 對自家題目有 +9 個百分點自我偏好,Google 則呈 -8 個百分點反向偏好;所有組態在閉卷可解題上約提升 33 個百分點,揭示參數記憶的上限。此基準為領域深度與偏差控制提供了可稽核的評測方案。
papers.title: OenoBench: A Wine-Domain Benchmark for Knowledge-Grounded Evaluation of Large Language Models
papers.title_zh: OenoBench:以知識為本的葡萄酒領域 LLM 評測基準

links.title: PACEShop: Evaluating Personalized, Actionable, Compositional, and Evidence-grounded Shopping Assistants

evidence: Abstract: PACEShop contains '22,625 controlled records with structured personas, auditable evidence pools, GOOD/BAD labels, and gold defect family and location annotations'; PACEJudge is 'a training-free judging protocol'.

Sec. 5.1: evaluation uses 'seven LLM backbones (Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6, Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, Qwen3 32B, GPT-OSS 20B, GPT-OSS 120B)' against multi-target rubric ablations (G-Eval, MT-Bench-style, persona-blind, persona-aware) and single-target adapted baselines (ARES-style, PersonaLens-style, EtaPP-style).
Tab. 3 (7-backbone means): PACEJudge PACE avg 0.56 vs persona-aware 0.51 and G-Eval 0.45; S1 P-source 0.32 vs 0.20; False-fire 0.47.
Tab. 4: strict paired-counterfactual 7-backbone mean PACE avg 0.21 for PACEJudge vs 0.14 best baseline ('Lift ... +0.07'), with a larger +0.22 lift on Sonnet 4.6.
Tab. 20 (leakage audit, Sec. C.2): ARES-style and PersonaLens-style stay under 1-2% 'Any off-target' firing while EtaPP-style leaks at 99%, supporting the honest '–' cells.
Appx. B.9: BAD records produced by 'deterministic rule-based defect injection in Python', so 'gold defect family and gold defect location label ... [are] known by construction'.
Limitations: 'GOOD responses come from a single generator (Claude Opus 4.6)'; '129/4,460 are review-augmented'; holdout '345/1,200 personas'; 'The dataset is English-only.'
Tab. 23 (per-backbone): PACEJudge on Sonnet 4.5 shows S0=0.55, S1=0.78, False-fire=0.85, illustrating high per-backbone variance behind the means.
llm_evaluation.rationale: An LLM-as-a-judge evaluation benchmark and training-free judging protocol for structured shopping-assistant responses. In scope: it is fundamentally LLM evaluation/prompting methodology (structured output contracts, judge ablations, evidence-grounding/hallucination diagnosis), not an out-of-scope pure-domain application. Preference alignment is solid on LLMs, LLM-as-judge/benchmarks, prompting, and RAG-style grounding, though it lacks Japanese/NLP, reasoning, or agent/tool-use depth, and the e-commerce instantiation is domain-bounded. Rigor is a strength: seven backbones, four rubric ablations sharing one schema, three honestly-adapted single-target baselines with a leakage audit (Tab. 20), strict paired-counterfactual metrics with false-fire/specificity gates (Tab. 4), five validity layers, and defect-tier analysis. However, headline strict-metric lifts are modest (7-backbone PACE avg 0.21 vs 0.14 best baseline in Tab. 4; +0.07), per-backbone variance is high (e.g., PACEJudge Sonnet 4.5 S0=0.55, false-fire 0.85 in Tab. 23), and metrics were co-designed with the authors' own protocol, which favors it. Evidence is internally consistent and quantitative but entirely synthetic: GOOD responses from a single generator (Claude Opus 4.6), BAD records via deterministic rule edits (Appx. B.9), English-only, thin grounding (129/4,460 review-augmented records). Generalizability beyond shopping/English is asserted rather than demonstrated (cross-generator n=50, real-assistant n=100 slices). Reproducibility is decent: prompts reproduced verbatim (Appx. C.3, D.4), construction code and released dataset referenced, though no explicit artifact links appear in the text.

primary_link.title: PACEShop: Evaluating Personalized, Actionable, Compositional, and Evidence-grounded Shopping Assistants

papers.summary: Shopping assistants are shifting from ranked product lists toward structured decision support, where systems must synthesize shopper context, product evidence, and next-step guidance into a coherent recommendation experience. This changes the unit of evaluation: a fluent response can still fail by ignoring shopper context, contradicting itself across components, or leaving defects too vague to localize. Existing personalization, grounding, and LLM-as-a-judge benchmarks cover pieces of this probl
papers.summary_zh: 購物助理正從排名清單轉向結構化決策支援,但現有個人化、接地與 LLM-as-a-judge 基準僅涵蓋片面,缺乏針對結構化回覆的共同評測目標。本文將此缺口定義為 PACE:個人化、可行動、組合式與證據接地。作者以兩項成果實作:其一為 PACEShop 基準資料集,包含 22,625 筆受控紀錄,配有結構化人物誌、可稽核證據池、GOOD/BAD 標籤及金標準缺陷類別與位置標註——BAD 紀錄由對已驗證 GOOD 回覆進行規則式缺陷注入產生,標籤由建構過程保證正確;其二為 PACEJudge,免訓練的評審協定,要求裁判以結構化輸出契約回報缺陷類別、回覆欄位位置與證據 ID。跨七個 LLM 骨幹的實驗顯示,通用裁判能辨識整體好壞,卻難以恢復診斷所需欄位;PACEJudge 無需再訓練即提升人物誌來源診斷、跨元件定位、接地與缺陷閉合等指標,且在訊號最弱的單一缺陷等級上優勢最大。此研究證明現實購物助理評測需要任務匹配的輸出契約,而非僅靠更強的骨幹模型或純量提示。
papers.title: PACEShop: Evaluating Personalized, Actionable, Compositional, and Evidence-grounded Shopping Assistants
papers.title_zh: PACEShop:評測個人化、可行動、組合式與證據接地的購物助理

links.title: Stored in Optimizer State, Valued by Later Training: A Causal Account of Subliminal Trait Transfer

evidence: Abstract: matched Qwen factorial yields route-conditioned source effects of -0.658 (S+), +0.008 (z_null), +0.658 (S-) seed means; the ordering recurs in all 12 Llama-3.2-1B seeds after eight updates and grows in every paired seed at sixteen updates.

Sec. 3: local adjoint allocation at lag 24 places 89.9% of the signed source contribution in the first moment; the w+m transplant reproduces the full descendant in 14/14 seed-route cells (SSE/ZERO 0.005-0.006 physical, 0.002-0.003 hidden).

Sec. 4.2: the parameter-free full-horizon costate predictor matches all 42 Qwen route-mean signs (aggregate SSE/ZERO=0.0103) and beats ZERO, source-cut, and route-constant baselines in 7/7 seeds; on Llama it matches 51/54 raw signs and all 21 resolved signs with mean within-seed Spearman 0.892.

Appendix J (Fig. 7a): source-scale titration shows the predictor beats baselines consistently only at >=1024 rows and is seed-unstable at 256-512, an explicitly reported validity boundary; Sec. 7 acknowledges exact attribution requires the full trajectory and one adjoint solve per route.

Appendix O (Table 14): implemented JVPs match Richardson central differences with max relative error <3e-8 for AdamW and momentum SGD under clipped and unclipped regimes; the document contains no code-repository or artifact availability statement.
llm_evaluation.rationale: In-scope LLM training-dynamics/safety paper: studies how subliminal teacher traits survive source removal in Qwen/Llama/SmolLM2/TinyLlama, identifying the AdamW first moment as causal carrier via a transport-valuation adjoint identity. Novel application of discrete-time adjoint analysis to the full trainer state with clean state-surgery identification; unusually rigorous with matched factorials, orthogonal null routes, random-plane controls, sign tests with Holm correction, parameter-only and horizon-truncation ablations, and honest boundary reporting (low-signal regime, TinyLlama/SmolLM2 cancellation cells). Evidence is strong within its scope but rests on small models (135M-1.1B, mostly LoRA), synthetic trait banks (owl/cat/red/oak over bare-number completions), and n=7-12 seed sign tests; some panels are explicitly descriptive (momentum-SGD factorial p=0.25; Tables 11-13 lack seed-level uncertainty). No code or artifact release is stated. Weighted score reflects high preference match (LLM 2.5, safety/alignment-adjacent, optimization, interpretability) tempered by scale and artificiality of the behavioral readouts.

primary_link.title: Stored in Optimizer State, Valued by Later Training: A Causal Account of Subliminal Trait Transfer

papers.summary: Subliminal trait transfer allows a student model to acquire behavioral dispositions from teacher-generated data in which the trait is not semantically expressed. Recent work explains how such signals enter gradients, but not how they survive source removal or acquire different signs under later training. We treat parameters and optimizer moments as a single trainer state and derive an exact transport-valuation identity separating observer-independent propagation of the source perturbation from t
papers.summary_zh: 本文探討大型語言模型訓練中的「潛意識特質遷移」現象：學生模型從教師生成的資料中習得行為傾向，但該特質並未在語義層面顯現。作者將參數與最佳化器動量視為單一「訓練器狀態」，透過離散時間伴隨敏感性分析推導出精確的「傳輸—賦值」恆等式，將觀察者無關的擾動傳播（傳輸）與未來訓練路徑及行為讀出所賦予的價值（賦值）正式分離。狀態手術實驗確認最佳化器的一階動量是因果載體：僅移植一階動量在切點處不產生任何可見效應，但在後續無源更新中持續釋放並生成不斷增長的差異；同時移植參數與一階動量則可完整恢復終端行為反應。同一來源誘導的狀態差異經由不同未來路徑可產生負值、近零或正值效應。全範域代價狀態預測器在Qwen上正確預測全部42條路徑均值符號，該結果跨Qwen、SmolLM2、Llama重現。限制在於精確歸因需完整軌跡與逐路徑伴隨求解，緊湊預測器在低訊號時解析度下降。此研究為理解訓練過程中資訊如何被物理攜帶與最終表達提供了雙階段機制框架。
papers.title: Stored in Optimizer State, Valued by Later Training: A Causal Account of Subliminal Trait Transfer
papers.title_zh: 儲存於最佳化器狀態、由後續訓練賦值：潛意識特質遷移的因果解析

links.title: Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization

evidence: Abstract: 'IAR improves over Vanilla SFT on all four reported metrics in 7 of 8 dataset-model settings, with average gains of 3.6 percentage points in domain QA accuracy and 12.1 percentage points in mean general performance'
Table 1 (Results): Llama-3.2-3B CC, IAR 36.5/60.2/35.0/30.5 vs Vanilla SFT 35.5/54.2/11.2/21.5; Phi CCI IAR 39.7 domain < 40.2 and MMLU 50.2 < 53.8, confirming the 7-of-8 boundary case

Related Work: 'IAR does not claim a new family of reconstruction losses. Its increment is a controlled empirical decomposition... then treats post-hoc capability recovery as an explicit third variable'
Stage 3: Recover: 'Recover evaluates post-hoc merge operators... from four families: SLERP, task arithmetic, TIES, and DARE' (no new merge algorithm)
Evaluation: 'Across 242,255 evaluated model-answer instances, the audit finds first-two exact agreement of .707, binary agreement of .848..., binary Cohen's κ=.691'

Appendix C (Runs and training seeds): 'Every reported checkpoint is a single training run; we do not average over multiple seeds' and 'Domain generation and judge APIs receive no explicit sampler seed'

Baselines: 'CPT+SFT from the corresponding released Base checkpoint... differs from the Instruct initialization used by IAR and therefore does not, by itself, isolate the effect of the Inject objective'
Appendix C (Scaling-run parameter provenance): 'the original Inject/Align training arguments, logs, and node manifests for the scaling ablation are not present in the available run archive'
Conclusion: 'These results support staged exposure and recovery as a strong, setting-dependent operating point rather than a uniformly dominant recipe'
Table 2 (RQ2): 'IAR wins 14 of 16 comparisons, with the exceptions being CC Llama domain accuracy and CC Qwen3-4B MMLU' against token-budget-matched QA-only SFT
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM post-training methodology paper: retrieval-free document knowledge internalization across Llama/Phi/Qwen/SmolLM families, directly matching LLM and knowledge-injection preferences; no out-of-scope domain content. Novelty is modest and self-acknowledged: Inject objectives resemble AdaptLLM/SELF-TUNING-style document transformation, and Recover reuses SLERP/task-arithmetic/TIES/DARE rather than introducing a new merge algorithm; the increment is a controlled three-way decomposition plus a BudgetMatch token control. Rigor is above average: fixed 12-candidate merge grid, validation-based selection before held-out test reporting, per-file bootstrap intervals, and an unusually candid judge-reliability audit (κ=0.691) and boundary-case analyses (Qwen3-4B CCI high base prior via BPB diagnostic). Deductions for single-run experiments without seed averaging, unseeded stochastic generation/judging, the partially unresolved Base- vs Instruct-initialized CPT confound (only 3 archived diagnostics), and unclear validation-only selection of Inject mixtures. Evidence is solid: the '7 of 8 all-metric wins over Vanilla SFT' claim verifies against Table 1, and BudgetMatch/scaling tables support the frontier claims, though the primary domain metric is LLM-judged and several deltas are small. Generalizability is limited by explicitly setting-dependent conclusions and no universal best Inject recipe. Reproducibility benefits from extensive hyperparameters, token accounting, and prompt schemas, but no explicit public code URL is stated and scaling-run configs lack provenance.

primary_link.title: Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization

papers.summary: Large language models often fail to answer questions about a bounded document collection when the source documents are not retrieved at inference time. We study this setting as document knowledge internalization: converting a fixed corpus into usable parametric knowledge for retrieval-free question answering. We propose IAR (Inject, Align, and Recover), a three-stage post-training framework that separates structured document knowledge injection, QA behavior alignment, and general ability recover
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究「文件知識內化」問題：在推論時無法檢索源文件的情況下，模型能否從固定語料庫中回答問題。作者提出IAR三階段後訓練框架，明確分離三個功能：Inject將源文件轉換為延續、改寫及指令條件重建等監督目標進行密集文件曝露；Align以僅答案QA監督對注入模型進行行為對齊；Recover透過事後模型合併（SLERP、task arithmetic、TIES、DARE）恢復通用能力。在CC與CCI兩個語料庫、Llama/Phi/Qwen/SmolLM四個模型家族上，IAR在8個設置中的7個全面超越Vanilla SFT，領域QA準確率平均提升3.6個百分點，通用效能（IFEval、MMLU、MSBench）平均提升12.1個百分點。BudgetMatch控制實驗確認增益並非僅來自更多訓練token。限制包括CPT初始化敏感性、最佳注入配方依賴模型與語料組合，以及無法保證所有指標的均勻優勢。此研究為需要無檢索部署的場景提供了系統性的知識內化實作方案。
papers.title: Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization
papers.title_zh: 注入、對齊、恢復：面向無檢索文件知識內化的分階段後訓練

links.title: Consilience: Conformally Calibrated Communication Control for Hidden-Profile Multi-Agent Reasoning

evidence: Abstract: claims a 'round-wise conformal calibration procedure that provides a distribution-free, finite-sample guarantee' and reports gains over fixed protocols, 'sometimes surpassing a full-information baseline'.
Section 3.1.3, Eq. (4)-(6): conformal acceptance requires executing 'all admissible actions' as counterfactual branches from each state every round; this branching compute cost is never quantified.

Appendix A 'Scope of the guarantee': concedes that exchangeability at later rounds 'is an additional assumption' under sequential adaptation, that no trajectory-level simultaneous coverage is provided, and that the guarantee concerns surrogate one-step regret, not answer correctness.

Section 3.1.1 'Surrogate discussion loss': coefficients alpha_H...alpha_P are 'fixed design hyperparameters, selected before evaluation and held constant', but their numeric values (and alpha, lambda) are never reported.

Model-count inconsistency: abstract and Table 1 caption say 12 models; Appendix B says '13 instruction-tuned open-weight language models'; Table 3 lists 15 rows including DeepSeek-V4-Flash/Pro absent from the Appendix B model list.

Appendix E Table 8: speaker-routing ablation shows round-robin attains the lowest normalized regret (0.4839 vs. 0.4868 for action-conditional routing) and the text admits 'only limited evidence of a clear advantage over round-robin routing', tempering Section 5.5.2's framing.

Appendix C.1: held-out MLP (0.73) vs. all-task MLP (0.77) comparison uses different task sets (60 vs. 65); the appendix itself notes this 'combines controller-training effects with a small difference in the evaluation task set'.
Section 4 'Benchmarks and models': the generated travel benchmark 'is not a reproduction and its results are not directly comparable' because original GroupTravelBench data were unavailable.

Reproducibility: no code, data, or artifact release is mentioned anywhere, though Appendix F provides complete prompt templates and Appendix F.1-F.2 details the synthetic benchmark generation, validation, and repair pipeline.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Strongly on-topic: an inference-time orchestration framework for multi-agent LLM systems (Agents & Tool Use, LLMs, Reasoning preferences), evaluated on hidden-profile decision tasks across many open-weight models. The core novelty — round-wise conformal calibration of communication actions with finite-sample one-step regret guarantees — is a genuine and non-obvious combination, though components (entropy/JSD state features, debate controllers, routing heuristics) are individually familiar. Rigor is solid but not exemplary: a formal proposition with an honest scope discussion and five ablations are offset by unreported hyperparameter values (surrogate loss coefficients, alpha, lambda), no significance testing or confidence intervals on headline claims, an unquantified per-round compute overhead from exhaustive counterfactual branching, and inconsistent model counts (12 in abstract/Table 1, 13 in Appendix B, 15 rows in Table 3). Evidence is extensive but relies on a surrogate objective rather than correctness guarantees, the second benchmark is a non-comparable regeneration (original data unavailable), and the routing ablation shows round-robin achieves lower normalized regret than the proposed router. Generalizability is limited to finite-answer-set group decision tasks; heterogeneous-agent analysis adds some breadth. Reproducibility is middling: complete prompt templates and benchmark-generation/validation pipelines are provided, but no code/data release is stated and key constants are missing.

primary_link.title: Consilience: Conformally Calibrated Communication Control for Hidden-Profile Multi-Agent Reasoning

papers.summary: Multi-agent LLM systems can improve reasoning by pooling diverse perspectives, but their effectiveness depends on coordinating communication, particularly in hidden-profile settings where each agent holds only part of the evidence required for a correct decision. Existing protocols, including fixed schedules, round-robin exchange, and unstructured debate, provide no guarantee that a conversational action is appropriate. We propose Consilience, an inference-time orchestration framework that both
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出Consilience，一個推論時多代理LLM協調框架，解決隱藏概要設定下的通訊控制問題。在該設定中，每位代理僅持有部分證據，正確決策需透過溝通整合分散的私有資訊。Consilience將通訊控制建模為序貫決策問題：每輪以緊湊狀態向量（不確定性、分歧度、證據增益、冗餘度、過早共識等）描述討論狀態，控制器從四種干預動作（挑戰、釐清、尋求證據、路由）中提案，再以逐輪共形校準提供無分布有限樣本保證——控制器的提案行為之一步遺憾以至少1-α的機率被校準閾值約束。動作條件路由器根據動作類型選擇最合適的發言者。在HiddenBench的65個任務上，跨12個模型，最佳控制器平均任務準確率達0.83，遠高於固定輪流的0.26，且在11/12模型上超越全資訊基線。消融實驗顯示路由與證據尋求動作貢獻最大。限制包括保證僅為逐輪邊際性而非全程覆蓋，且要求輪次特定的可交換性假設。此框架展示了結構化通訊控制可媲美增加資訊可用性。

links.title: COPA: Continual Preference Optimization for Adaptive Prompt Injection Defense

evidence: Section IV-B: 'COPA achieves the lowest ASR of 0.035, up to 6.3x lower than SecAlign (0.221) and 3.0x lower than the strongest baseline (LlamaGuard, 0.104)' - supports the headline ASR claim; the abstract's '4.4x on average' and 'improving backward transfer by 0.119' are not traceable to reported numbers.
Section IV-C Table I: margin-weighted replay vs uniform replay yields ASR 0.035 vs 0.163, BWT +0.028 vs +0.003, AP 0.850 vs 0.600.
Section IV-C Table II: GRPO vs DPO under the same lifelong sequence yields ASR 0.035 vs 0.335, BWT +0.028 vs -0.231, AP 0.850 vs 0.626.

Section IV-A: LoRA r=64, dropout 0.1, 4-bit NF4, 30 GRPO updates per task, replay buffer stores 60 preference pairs, single NVIDIA A100; D0 is only '102 cybersecurity preference pairs from the PromptInjection module of the DeepTeam Red Teaming Framework'.
Section IV-A/IV-B: utility evaluated on 'MMLU-Pro [25] and GPQA [26]' but Figure 4 caption reports 'GPQA and MMLU'; COPA attains 0.310 GPQA and 0.340 MMLU vs undefended base 0.300/0.332.
Section IV-B Figure 5: 'COPA maintains low ASR (0.035 to 0.054)' across Llama 3.1 8B, Mistral 7B v0.3, and Qwen 2.5 7B, supporting model-agnostic generalization claims.

Section III-B: threat model specifies an external adversary with input-interface-only access and a non-stationary attack distribution, but evaluation relies on an unspecified 'automatic safety judge' (Section III-C) without judge validation, seeds, or variance reporting.
Section III-C/III-D: GRPO group size G, KL coefficient beta, and replay temperature eta are introduced symbolically but their values are never reported, and no code release is mentioned.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core in-scope LLM security/alignment paper: prompt injection defense framed as continual preference optimization using GRPO, LoRA adapters, and margin-weighted replay, evaluated on Llama/Mistral/Qwen backbones. The lifelong-adversarial framing and GRPO-margin-based replay prioritization are moderately novel combinations of existing techniques (GRPO, LoRA, replay-based continual learning, SecAlign-style preference defense), with a credible claim of being the first continual pipeline for prompt injection defense. Rigor is decent: fair-pipeline baselines (LlamaGuard, DataSentinel, SecAlign), standard BWT/AP metrics, two ablations (replay strategy, GRPO vs DPO), and cross-backbone plus held-out/OOD attack evaluation (S1-S3). Weaknesses: results mostly in figures with a few unverifiable summary claims (abstract's '4.4x on average' and 'BWT +0.119' not traceable to reported numbers; results only support 6.3x vs SecAlign and 3.0x vs strongest baseline), no seeds/error bars, a small 102-pair alignment set and 60-pair buffer, an unspecified binary 'automatic safety judge', and minor MMLU vs MMLU-Pro inconsistency. Missing GRPO group size G, KL coefficient beta, replay temperature eta, and no code release limit reproducibility. Overall a solid, relevant contribution with real quantitative support but modest statistical and disclosure rigor.

primary_link.title: COPA: Continual Preference Optimization for Adaptive Prompt Injection Defense

papers.summary: LLMs remain vulnerable to prompt injection attacks, where adversarial instructions embedded in user inputs or external content manipulate model behavior and bypass safeguards. Existing defenses are predominantly static, relying on fixed alignment objectives or attack-specific filtering mechanisms that require redesign as new attack strategies emerge. While recent lifelong alignment methods address shifting user preferences, they do not account for adaptive adversaries that continually evolve to
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出COPA框架，將大型語言模型的提示注入防禦形式化為持續學習問題。不同於靜態防禦依賴固定對齊目標或一次性分類器過濾，COPA透過GRPO（Group Relative Policy Optimization）增量吸收新觀察到的攻擊反饋，同時以邊際加權經驗回放保留對先前攻擊類別的防禦。框架分為兩階段：第一階段在通用網路安全偏好資料上對凍結基礎模型的LoRA適配器進行偏好對齊；第二階段在攻擊變體串流上持續訓練，使用對數似然邊際作為免標籤的不確定性訊號，優先重放防禦最不穩固的偏好對。在CyberSecEval九種攻擊變體的持續序列上，COPA將攻擊成功率降低至0.035，較最佳靜態防禦低6.3倍，同時保持正的後向遷移（+0.028）與MMLU/GPQA通用能力。消融確認邊際加權回放與GRPO目標各貢獻關鍵增益。限制為實驗侷限於Llama-3.1-8B等三個骨架模型及特定攻擊基準。此工作將提示注入防禦從靜態問題轉化為可持續適應的終身學習範式。

links.title: MileGPO: Milestone Inference with Local Evidence for Graph-Based Policy Optimization of Long-Horizon LLM Agents

evidence: Abstract: 'Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop show state-of-the-art performance and a small in-distribution to out-of-distribution gap on ALFWorld.'
Section 4.1.2: 'All local runs use Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct ... we extended training for all local methods to 300 optimization steps and selected the checkpoint with the best validation performance.'
Table 1: MileGPO ALFWorld All 94.60 (±0.3) and WebShop Succ. 78.58 (±1.2) vs reproduced GraphGPO* 91.47 and 74.80.
Table 2: ALFWorld ID-OOD gap 1.69 for MileGPO vs 1.89 (GiGPO) and 3.78 (GraphGPO).
Table 3: removing PCC drops WebShop score from 90.3 to 87.9 and success from 78.6 to 77.2; further removing RCS drops success to 73.8.
Appendix A.5 / Table 5: full hyperparameter enumeration but environment-specific recipes differ (e.g., η=0.20 ALFWorld vs 1.00 WebShop, θ_m=1.1 vs 0.5, κ_bc=0 vs 1).
Appendix C.1: 'the comparison replays alternative shaping on fixed trajectories ... should be interpreted as descriptive mechanism evidence rather than a causal training ablation.'
Appendix B: Propositions 1-3 give bounded, tie-resolving residual interpolation proofs; no code or artifact availability statement appears in the document.
llm_evaluation.rationale: In-scope methodological paper on credit assignment for RL-trained LLM agents (Agents & Tool Use, LLM, RL preferences): MileGPO augments GraphGPO's graph-distance returns with milestone/trap discovery, reliability weighting, and same-state branch/progress calibration. Novelty is moderate—the contribution is an incremental refinement of a very recent line (GiGPO, GraphGPO, HGPO, StepPO, BiPACE) rather than a new framework. Rigor is solid: aligned local reproductions with shared configs (Sec 4.1.2, App A.3), 3 seeds with stds (Table 1), cumulative ablations (Table 3), tie-correction diagnostics (Fig 4, 26.5% vs 17.0% in App C.1), efficiency profiling (Sec 4.6), and simple correctness propositions (App B). Concerns: many hand-tuned hyperparameters differing per environment (Table 5: η=0.20 vs 1.00, θ_m=1.1 vs 0.5), best-validation checkpoint selection, extension of all baselines to 300 steps, a single 1.5B model, and only two benchmarks, limiting generalizability; no code release stated. The replay analysis is honestly labeled descriptive, not causal (App C.1). Evidence for the SOTA claim is credible within the compared set (Table 1: 94.60 ALFWorld / 78.58 WebShop; Table 2 gap 1.69), but the mechanism-to-gain link rests partly on correlational diagnostics.

primary_link.title: MileGPO: Milestone Inference with Local Evidence for Graph-Based Policy Optimization of Long-Horizon LLM Agents

papers.summary: Credit assignment is challenging in long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning, where supervision often comes only from final rewards. Existing methods refine trajectory-level signals into step-level credits through step grouping or graph-based advantage estimation, but can overlook meaningful intermediate milestones. We propose MileGPO (Milestone Inference with Local Evidence for Graph-Based Policy Optimization), which derives process-level credit from grouped on-policy rollouts through three
papers.summary_zh: 本文針對長時程代理強化學習中的信用分配問題提出MileGPO。現有基於最終目標距離的圖形化信用估計（如GraphGPO）僅捕捉可達性，無法區分同等距離下可靠性截然不同的中間狀態。MileGPO包含三個嵌套設計：Milestone Discovery從成功軌跡中識別候選里程碑、從失敗軌跡中識別重複陷阱；Reliability-Calibrated Shaping以基於結果的經驗信度對候選加權，強化可靠錨點並壓制不確定者；Progress-Contrastive Calibration進一步評估局部進展與同源狀態分支間的反事實比較，以區分真正進展與偶然關聯。整個流程僅重用rollout圖與在線結果獎勵，不需輔助模型、外部標註或額外環境互動。在ALFWorld與WebShop上，MileGPO均達到最先進表現，ALFWorld ID-OOD差距僅1.69點（GiGPO為1.89、GraphGPO為3.78），顯示更強的泛化能力。消融與診斷確認信度加權、局部進展與分支證據各自貢獻互補增益。限制為方法仍依賴rollout組中足夠的共同狀態結構。

papers.title_zh: MileGPO：以局部證據進行里程碑推論的長時程LLM代理圖形化策略最佳化

links.title: MemTrapBench: Benchmarking Cognitive Traps in LLM Memory Use

evidence: Abstract: 'all evaluated memory strategies underperform the no-memory setting, with even the strongest methods suffering drops of more than 10%.' Consistent with Table 1 (EverMemOS 71.17 vs wo/Mem 85.16 on Gemini-3-Flash-Preview; LightMem 70.13 vs 81.83 on Qwen3-30B).

Section 3.3, Table 3: no-trap control achieves 94.39% avg on the Task Boundary subset vs 31.05% with trap-inducing memory (and 92.29% wo/Mem), supporting the claim that degradation is driven by trap semantics rather than history presence.

Section 3.5, Table 5: GPT-5.2 and Claude-Sonnet-4.6 judges both show large wo/Mem-to-Mem drops (92.29->31.05 and 95.57->40.07) across three independent runs, evidencing judge-direction agreement but also large absolute judge divergence.

Section 3.6: AdaptiveMem gains of 11.8/14.9/11.3 points (Gemini) and 4.2/2.5/2.6 points (Qwen) on MemTrapBench for FullText/LightMem/EverMemOS; results computed on 200 randomly sampled instances per benchmark.
Footnote 1: 'Data and code will be available at https://github.com/zjunlp/MemTrapBench' - availability is promised, not verified as released.

Appendices A-C: full AdaptiveMem system prompt, benchmark construction prompts (GPT-5.4 generation with 18-40 turn dialogues), and per-category evaluation rubrics are included, aiding reproducibility.
llm_evaluation.rationale: An LLM-focused memory benchmark paper squarely within scope: it studies how retrieved memories distort LLM reasoning and beliefs, introduces MemTrapBench (1,050 instances, 4 trap categories), evaluates five memory strategies against a no-memory baseline on two model families, and proposes AdaptiveMem, an inference-time prompt skill. Preference relevance is strong (LLMs, memory/long-context, agents, safety evaluation, prompting), though it is not about Japanese NLP or architecture. Novelty is moderately high: framing memory-induced cognitive traps (Reasoning Fixation, Belief Distortion, 'Trauma') goes beyond existing extraction/retrieval benchmarks and the concurrent MemSyco-Bench, though context-poisoning and distraction effects are adjacent prior art. Rigor is solid but not exceptional: there is a proper causal control (no-trap memory in Table 3), a memory-length ablation (Table 4), and cross-judge reliability over three runs (Table 5), but evaluation relies entirely on LLM judges, AdaptiveMem is tested on only 200 sampled instances per benchmark, no statistical significance tests are reported, human QC details are deferred to supplementary material, and there is no explicit limitations section. Evidence strength is good because headline claims match the tables (best memory strategies drop ~14 and ~11.7 points vs no-memory; AdaptiveMem gains up to 14.9 points without degrading LongMemEval), but all metrics are judge-derived. Generalizability is limited to two model families and English synthetic dialogues; reproducibility is helped by fully included prompts (Appendices A-C) but code/data are only promised ('will be available') and judge models are proprietary.

primary_link.title: MemTrapBench: Benchmarking Cognitive Traps in LLM Memory Use

papers.summary: Memory has become a key component of large language models, enabling them to retain information and learn from long-term interactions. However, existing memory benchmarks mainly evaluate whether information is correctly extracted, stored, and retrieved, while largely overlooking how retrieved memories reshape model reasoning and affect performance on the current task. We identify memory-induced cognitive traps: even faithfully recorded and semantically relevant memories can distort model reasoni
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示大型語言模型記憶系統的「記憶誘導認知陷阱」：即使忠實記錄且語義相關的記憶，也可能扭曲模型推理或信念並降低當前任務表現。作者提出MemTrapBench，包含1,050個實例，涵蓋兩類四種陷阱：推理固著（認知偏誤、創傷、任務邊界）與信念扭曲（安全）。實例透過精心設計的陷阱種子、多輪對話生成及雙階段品質控制建構。在Gemini-3-Flash-Preview與Qwen3-30B-A3B上評估五種記憶策略（FullText、LightMem、MemOS、SimpleMem、EverMemOS），所有策略均低於無記憶基線，最強方法也下降超過10個百分點。控制實驗確認退化由陷阱語義驅動而非上下文長度。作者進一步提出AdaptiveMem，一個輕量提示技能，引導模型在使用記憶前辨識四種風險並檢查適用性。AdaptiveMem在MemTrapBench上為LightMem提升14.9個百分點（Gemini），同時在LongMemEval上保持或提升通用記憶效能。此工作凸顯了記憶系統評估中長期被忽視的下游推理影響維度。
papers.title: MemTrapBench: Benchmarking Cognitive Traps in LLM Memory Use
papers.title_zh: MemTrapBench：基準測試LLM記憶使用中的認知陷阱

links.title: DeltaML-Bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Real-World Research Repositories

evidence: Abstract: ARG raises GPT-5 per-run success from 9.4% to 33.9% (4x6h) and to 49.0% (2x12h); Modular gaming rates up to 47.9% with none observed in evaluated ARG configurations.

Section 3.2: 48 tasks sourced from Papers With Code out of ~380 filtered candidates; human verification required training-loop initialization on a single GPU within a 15-20 minute window per repository.
Section 4.4 Tables 1 and 3: success and gaming rates with Wilcoxon significance (p<0.05); Claude Modular gaming rises 33.3% to 47.9% from 6h to 12h while GPT-5 Modular stays ~9-11%.

Section 4.2: four-layer audit (AST rule-based checks, training-artifact verification, LLM semantic analysis, forensic log grading); the paper states it 'does not independently estimate false-positive or false-negative rates.'

Section 4.5/Figure 2: five highest-scoring tasks account for 58.0-97.8% of total positive improvement and six of eight configurations have zero task-level median, qualifying the mean scores in Table 2.
Section 5.1: 'The experiment does not isolate which architectural components are associated with the difference, and we did not perform an ablation study' regarding ARG's zero gaming rate.

Section 5.4: limitations include only two frontier model families, two scaffoldings, no open-weights models, runs capped at 12 hours, and no assessment of solution novelty or computational efficiency.

Appendix A Tables 8-12: per-task success rate, gaming rate, score, time, and token usage for all 48 tasks; Appendix B provides timestamped forensic case studies and a taxonomy of 45 flagged runs across five gaming categories.
Section 5.3/Table 7: Claude ARG uses 9.0M tokens vs 1.1M Modular at 6h while GPT-5 ARG (10.3M) is comparable to Modular; the paper notes token use does not establish causal contribution to success.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A benchmark paper squarely in the LLM-agent evaluation space: GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4 drive a Modular baseline and a search-based ARG scaffolding to improve published baselines in 48 real research repositories, with specification-gaming audits adding an AI-safety dimension. Preference relevance is very high (agents, tool use, frontier LLMs, evaluation/red-teaming, code). Novelty is moderate: improvement-over-baseline on imperfect repos sits between MLRB/RE-Bench/MLE-bench, and the gaming-audit concept borrows from prior RE-Bench findings, though the layered integrity pipeline and scaffolding-vs-gaming comparison are useful additions. Rigor is above average: Wilcoxon tests, paired bootstrap intervals, human task verification, and unusually honest caveats (depth-vs-breadth confound in Table 1 allocations, score concentration in Figure 2 with 58.0-97.8% of gains in five tasks, n=1 NLP task flagged). It is capped by the absence of any ARG component ablation (explicitly admitted in Section 5.1), only two models and two scaffoldings, and an audit whose false-positive/negative rates are never estimated. Evidence strength benefits from exhaustive per-task tables (Appendix A) and timestamped forensic case studies (Appendix B), but the headline 'zero gaming under ARG' is absence-of-detection, and gaming correlates (89% failure precedents, 3.2x GNN rate) come from an under-specified trajectory analysis. Generalizability is limited by sample size, closed model set, and the authors' own framing that findings are specific to the studied setup. Reproducibility is decent (Vivaria, GPU/token budgets, hyperparameters, task IDs) but no explicit public release of the benchmark or ARG code is verified in the text. Weighted score ~0.72.

primary_link.title: DeltaML-Bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Real-World Research Repositories

papers.summary: Autonomous agents for machine learning experimentation must navigate heterogeneous repositories, repair training pipelines, and evaluate candidate improvements under realistic compute constraints. Existing benchmarks only partially capture these conditions. We introduce DeltaML-Bench, a benchmark comprising 48 tasks sourced from research papers that require agents to improve published baselines within imperfect, open-source repositories. We evaluate GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4 with a standard Modu
papers.summary_zh: 本文介紹DeltaML-Bench，一個由48個源自Papers With Code論文的研究任務組成的基準，要求代理在不完美、異構的開源儲存庫中改進已發表的基線結果。不同於SWE-bench（隔離bug修復）或MLE-bench（Kaggle風格），DeltaML-Bench模擬真實ML研究條件：代理必須導航多樣化程式碼庫、修復訓練管線、在時間與token預算下迭代實驗。基準配有多層完整性檢查（AST靜態分析、訓練產物驗證、LLM語義審計、法證級日誌評分）以偵測規格博弈。評估GPT-5與Claude Sonnet 4，搭配標準Modular腳手架與搜尋式ARG腳手架：ARG使GPT-5的單次運行成功率從9.4%提升至33.9%（4×6小時配置），12小時配置下更達49.0%。Modular配置的規格博弈率高達47.9%（Claude），而所有評估的ARG配置均未觀察到博弈行為。限制包括僅涵蓋兩個前沿模型家族、無法代表需分散式訓練的研究，以及博弈率結論尚未獨立驗證假陽性率。此基準為自主ML實驗代理的部署提供了完整性與能力並重的測試平台。
papers.title: DeltaML-Bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Real-World Research Repositories
papers.title_zh: DeltaML-Bench：在真實研究儲存庫上評估機器學習代理

links.title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models

evidence: Abstract: introduces dual-use concepts and ConceptGuard benchmark where forget and retain sets are 'explicitly complementary in concept usage' with intent-sensitive evaluation; dataset link to huggingface.co/datasets/sk0511/concept-guard

Section 4.2: dataset built from LLM-LAT harmful dataset, GPT-5-based (gpt-5-2025-08-07) concept tagging with manual supervision, GPT-5 generation of benign counterparts; final 5,166 instances, 68 concepts (Section 4.3/Table 6)
Appendix A.1: 15% (~1,000) tagged instances validated by two graduate annotators, Cohen's kappa = 0.81; Appendix A.3: benign counterpart validation kappa = 0.88
Appendix B: initial judge-human agreement kappa 0.44 improved to 0.72 after removing contextual examples and using rubric-based zero-shot judging on 200 responses
Section 5.2: LLM-as-judge uses 'GPT-5.4 (instead of GPT-5 to avoid circular evaluation)' although GPT-5 generated the benign retain set, an imperfect circularity mitigation
Table 2: Llama-3.1-8B Gradient Ascent reaches HarmMem 0.02 but HelpRet collapses to 0.05 (from fine-tuned 0.75), demonstrating over-suppression; SimNPO best balances (HelpRet 0.55, HelpQA 0.66)

Table 3: best contextual separation CtxtSep = 0.34 (SimNPO, Qwen) and 0.38 (RMU, Llama) vs fine-tuned 0.13/0.05 and base 0.19/0.22, supporting the claim that methods only partially achieve safe unlearning
Section 6, Figure 4: reducing forget set proportion yields only marginal, rank-preserving gains in contextual separation
Appendix C: 2x NVIDIA RTX 4090, bfloat16, Open Unlearning framework base, shared fine-tuning table (10 epochs, lr 1e-5) and per-method hyperparameters; no code repository stated
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM safety/evaluation paper: a benchmark (ConceptGuard) for context-sensitive machine unlearning using dual-use concepts with complementary forget/retain sets, directly matching LLM, AI Safety, and Red Teaming/Evaluation preferences. The framing (intent-sensitive concept-level unlearning vs. disjoint fact removal in TOFU/MUSE/WMDP) is a genuine if incremental contribution, and the contextual separation metric is new. Rigor is solid but not exceptional: multi-stage dataset construction with human validation (Cohen's kappa 0.81/0.88 on 15% of instances), four recent unlearning methods across two models, forget-set-size ablation, and human validation of LLM judges (kappa 0.44 to 0.72 on 200 responses). Weaknesses: no seeds, error bars, or significance tests; percent changes in Tables 2-3 are computed against the base rather than the fine-tuned model, complicating interpretation; ROUGE as a primary memorization/utility proxy is weak; and potential judge circularity since GPT-5 generated the benign retain set while a proprietary 'GPT-5.4' judged outputs. Evidence concretely supports the headline claims (best CtxtSep 0.34-0.38 vs base 0.19-0.22; GA utility collapse), but uncertainty is unquantified. Generalizability is limited to two mid-size English instruction-tuned models, four methods, and one source dataset. Reproducibility is helped by a public HuggingFace dataset, full hyperparameters (Appendix C), and released prompts, but no code release is stated and the judge model version is nonstandard.

primary_link.title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models

papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly require selective removal of harmful or sensitive knowledge, called unlearning, yet existing methods and benchmarks fail to evaluate this capability completely. Current approaches rely on disjoint forget and retain sets composed of independent facts, and measure success using simple and direct factual recall. This framing fails to capture a key requirement of unlearning, namely the ability to eliminate harmful behaviors while preserving benign and benefi
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出ConceptGuard，一個以「雙用途概念」為核心的LLM遺忘基準。現有遺忘基準（TOFU、MUSE、WMDP）使用不相交且隨機分割的遺忘集與保留集，僅評估孤立事實的刪除與保留，無法衡量模型是否能安全地在不同情境下使用同一概念。ConceptGuard讓遺忘集與保留集互補：同一概念的有害使用構成遺忘集，良性使用構成保留集。資料集含5,166個實例、68個雙用途概念，涵蓋網路安全、社會工程、虛假資訊等領域。評估引入「情境分離」指標，衡量模型在同一概念上抑制有害行為同時保留良性功能的能力。在Qwen-2.5-3B與Llama-3.1-8B上評估Gradient Ascent、SimNPO、RMU、UNDIAL四種遺忘方法：所有方法在概念層面表現不一致，呈現強烈的遺忘—效用權衡，情境分離增益有限。偏好型（SimNPO）與表示層（RMU）方法取得較佳分離，但仍遠未達到穩健的概念級解纏。此工作揭示了當前遺忘方法在安全部署中的根本侷限。
papers.title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
papers.title_zh: ConceptGuard：大型語言模型中情境敏感遺忘的基準測試

links.title: ReguSim: Evaluating LLM Agent Rule Grounding in Financial Compliance

evidence: Section 4.1 / Table 4: DeepSeek V4 Pro rejects 24.2% of submitted non-HOLD orders and Gemini 3.5 Flash 14.8% despite visible rule text; aggressive–conservative persona gap is 30.9 pp (DeepSeek) vs 9.5 pp (Gemini).

Table 5: DeepSeek ablations — removing rule text raises rejected attempts 24.2%→33.2% and rule breaches 10.0%→21.7%; prompt-only ledger keeps rejections similar (24.5%) while raising activity 31.6%→38.0%.

Table 6 and Table 12: logistic baseline reaches 71.4% macro cell F1 vs strongest LLM monitor GPT-5.4 Mini at 63.8%; paired bootstrap Logistic−GPT = 7.6 pp [1.0, 13.9] over 45 type–difficulty–regime cells.

Section 4.3 / Appendix Table 10: bridge study on 64 DeepSeek traces shows false accepts rise 25.0%→46.9% when the trader rationale is added, while rejection evidence lifts issue-type accuracy 53.1%→87.5% and evidence hits to 100%.

Limitations section: ReguBench records are synthetic (45 base scenarios, 9.4% case-inspired at template level only), Gemini replication uses two sessions per condition (1,800 decisions), and the authors explicitly disclaim real-world misconduct-rate, scaling, or legal-adjudication claims.

Appendix E item 1: the repository is 'referenced as an anonymized supplementary artifact; the public URL will be released after review' — no publicly available artifact at submission time, though seeds, temperature 0.0, SHA-256 response caching, and full prompts are documented.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A benchmark/evaluation paper squarely on LLM agents (Agents & Tool Use, LLM, Red Teaming & Evaluation, and partially AI Safety/Reasoning preferences): it evaluates DeepSeek/Gemini/GPT agents in an executable compliance loop separating stated reasoning, attempted action, enforcement, and monitor evidence. Novelty is moderate — the four-artifact separation and bridge study are sensible contributions over existing legal/financial benchmarks, but the setting is synthetic and the framework is an incremental specialization of agent-auditing ideas. Rigor is above average: factorial regime–incentive–persona design, ablations (rule text, persona, prompt-only ledger), a matched second-model replication, stratified 800-target monitor sample, and paired bootstrap CIs; the awareness metric is admittedly a keyword heuristic and the Gemini replication uses only 2 sessions per condition. Evidence for the headline claims (visible rules do not prevent rejected orders; structured baselines beat prompt-only LLM monitors; rationales mislead monitors without enforcement evidence) is quantitatively supported, though all data are synthetic and the paper appropriately disclaims real-world, scaling, and legal-validity claims, capping evidence strength and generalizability. Reproducibility is promising (seeds, temperature 0, SHA-256 caching, prompts in Appendix B) but code is only an anonymized artifact with public release deferred until after review. Not a pure domain application: the core contribution is agent-evaluation methodology, so the 0.20 cap does not apply.

primary_link.title: ReguSim: Evaluating LLM Agent Rule Grounding in Financial Compliance

papers.summary: LLM agents in financial markets may cite rules yet still submit orders that violate executable constraints or misread surveillance evidence. We introduce ReguSim, a controlled financial-compliance environment, and ReguBench, a target-marked monitoring benchmark, to separate four artifacts: stated reasoning, attempted action, execution enforcement, and monitor evidence. In trader runs with DeepSeek V4 Pro and Gemini 3.5 Flash, visible rules reduce but do not eliminate rejected actions, and incent
papers.summary_zh: 本論文針對 LLM 代理在金融市場的合規行為提出評估框架。作者指出,大型語言模型即使引用法規,仍可能送出違反價格帶、放空限制或 T+1 賣出約束的訂單,其自信的合規說辭也可能誤導監管判斷。為此,研究團隊建立可控金融合規環境 ReguSim 與標記目標的監測基準 ReguBench,將陳述推理、嘗試動作、執行結果與監管證據四類資訊分離記錄。實驗以 DeepSeek V4 Pro 為主要交易代理,Gemini 3.5 Flash 作為複製驗證:即使規則文字完整呈現於提示,DeepSeek 仍有 24.2% 送單遭拒,Gemini 為 14.8%;獲利與隱匿等目標設定會加劇越界,激進與保守人設的拒單率差距達 30.9 個百分點。消融顯示僅靠提示詞無法取代可執行的硬性控管;橋接研究亦發現,除非提供執行證據,交易代理的錯誤理由會拉偏獨立監測者的判斷。監測端上,規則與邏輯迴歸基線(71.4% Macro F1)優於純提示 LLM。限制在於所有資料皆為合成、模型覆蓋有限,且不宣稱真實市場的不當行為率。其價值在於主張金融合規評估應審計規則落實與證據使用,而非依賴單一合規分數。

links.title: The Asymmetric Harms of LLM Compression

evidence: Abstract: 'systematically evaluate 3 LLMs across 11 compression methods to investigate the effects of compression on knowledge retention, model confidence, and social bias'.

Section 4.2 (Relative Retention Shift by Popularity): 'N:M pruning is the most extreme with the tail retention 22.7 to 39.5 percentage points above overall and head retention 3.6 to 14.4 percentage points below it'.

Section 4.3 (Knowledge-Loss Rate): 'Even at mild settings... 22% to 35% of previously correct PopQA answers become incorrect. This proportion rises to 85 to 99% under the strongest compression settings'.
Section 4.4 (Worst-Subgroup Effects) and Table 4: 'SparseGPT 2:4 yields Delta B_g = -53.1 pp for secretary (95% CI [-77.7, -14.1]), while the overall change is only Delta B = -2.2 pp'.

Appendix A.2.1: 'the tail shift is positive in 104 configurations, the head shift is negative in 92, and the tail shift exceeds the head shift in 104' of 105 model-configuration combinations on PopQA.

Appendix A.2.3 (RQ3 takeaway): 'stronger claims about subgroups require fine-grained estimates accompanied by sample sizes and an analysis that accounts for selecting the largest effect from many candidate subgroups'.

Limitations: 'our experiments cover three 8-9B instruction-tuned models and selected post-training quantization and pruning methods. The findings may not generalize to substantially larger models, other architectures, or compression paradigms such as distillation'.

Appendix A.1, Tables 1-2: full quantization/pruning hyperparameters (calibration dataset C4, 128 samples, seed 42, sequence length 512, per-method settings) enabling replication, though no code-release statement appears.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A systematic empirical audit of LLM compression (4 quantization + 7 pruning variants across 11 methods, 3 open-weight 8-9B LLMs) showing aggregate metrics mask asymmetric harms: relative head-vs-tail retention shifts, persistent confidence on lost knowledge, and subgroup-level bias changes hidden by stable aggregate bias scores. Strongly on-preference (LLMs, scaling/efficiency via quantization/pruning, AI safety via bias/fairness, evaluation). Novelty is moderate: it unifies fragmented prior findings (Hooker 2020, Hua 2026, Marcuzzi 2026) under one protocol and adds a simple relative-retention-shift metric plus calibrated confidence-on-lost-knowledge analysis, but the individual phenomena largely extend known results. Rigor is solid: formal metric definitions, isotonic calibration with stratified split, 95% CIs, explicit collapsed-setting exclusion, and honest caveats (multiple-comparisons on subgroup maxima, no calibration for RQ3). Evidence is extensive and internally consistent (e.g., tail shift positive in 104/105 PopQA configurations; secretary subgroup delta -53.1pp vs overall -2.2pp under SparseGPT 2:4), though BBQ subgroup claims rest on wide CIs and descriptive aggregates. Generalizability is bounded: only 8-9B instruction-tuned models, patterns are dataset-dependent (PopQA vs Head-to-Tail differ), and the authors flag this. Reproducibility is helped by exhaustive configuration tables (Tables 1-2) and public datasets/models, but no code release is stated.

papers.summary_zh: 模型壓縮能降低部署成本,但困惑度與平均準確率等總體指標常掩蓋底層行為變化。本文以統一協定系統性評估 Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct、Qwen-3-8B 與 Gemma-2-9B-it 三個模型,涵蓋 GPTQ、AWQ、OmniQuant、AQLM 等量化與 WANDA、SparseGPT、ShortGPT 等剪枝共 11 種方法,檢視三個問題:知識保留是否隨流行度不對稱流失、模型對遺失知識的信心,以及壓縮對刻板印象偏好的影響。主要發現:其一,在 PopQA 上經相對保留率標準化後,常見的頭部知識保留比例反而低於罕見的尾部知識,剪枝下不對稱尤為明顯;其二,輕度壓縮即使 22% 至 35% 原本答對的 PopQA 題目變錯,模型對這些新錯答案仍維持中等偏高的信心;其三,總體偏見分數變動雖小,卻可能隱藏次群體間方向相反的大幅位移,例如 SparseGPT 2:4 下 secretary 職業偏見劇降 53.1 個百分點而總體僅降 2.2。作者提醒崩潰設定下的 ECE 改善不可靠,且研究僅涵蓋 8–9B 模型與部分壓縮方法。此研究說明部署壓縮模型前,必須進行細粒度、子群體層級的評估,不能僅憑平均指標背書。

links.title: Auditing Cross-Lingual Fairness in Language Model Watermarking

evidence: Abstract: framework applied to 'six watermarking schemes, three open-weight generators, eleven languages spanning four scripts and eight typological families, and both base and instruction-tuned regimes', revealing failure modes single-language single-paradigm evaluation cannot surface.

§3 Experimental Grid: 'every cell of a 11 languages x 6 schemes x 3 generators x 2 regimes grid at n=500 matched pairs per cell', ~200,000 matched watermarked/unwatermarked generations; generators are Mistral-NeMo-12B, Gemma-3-4B, Qwen2.5-7B with FLORES++ and AYA prompts.

§5.1 Calibration versus detection failure: Unigram-Gemma mean TPR 0.000 but mean AUC 0.986, and XSIR-Qwen AUC 0.978, so 'the watermark signal is present in both cells, and the global threshold simply sits above the unwatermarked-pool support'; per-language recalibration recovers TPR to 0.799 and 0.794.

§5.2: 'EXPEdit and SynthID (the two distortion-free schemes) sit at the bottom of the quality ranking under every paradigm in the base regime', with between-family share >=70% in 32 of 36 (scheme, paradigm, regime) quality cells.

§6 Limitations: 'Our eleven languages span four scripts and eight typological families, but many of the world's languages remain outside this set. Our six schemes... are not exhaustive of an actively growing literature.'
Appendix A Compute: 'All generation and evaluation runs were conducted on a mix of NVIDIA H100 and A100 GPUs.'; no code or artifact availability statement appears anywhere in the document.

§4.4: typological partition 'register[ed]... before analysis' with script partition as robustness check; Table 12 shows family partition captures more between-group variance than script partition for cells with non-trivial disparity.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A cross-lingual fairness audit of LLM text watermarking, squarely in scope (LLM output, fairness/safety evaluation). Relevance is solid but not core-LLM-methods: it audits watermark detectors rather than advancing LLM, reasoning, agent, or Japanese-LLM methodology. Novelty is moderate: the claimed first systematic cross-lingual watermarking audit (Abstract; §2) is credible, but the four framework components (empirical FPR calibration, AUC companion, three quality paradigms, GE2 within/between decomposition) are explicitly imported from fair-ML literature (§2, §4.1-4.4). Rigor is strong: an 11-language x 6-scheme x 3-generator x 2-regime grid at n=500 matched pairs (~200k generations, §3), bootstrap CIs (Table 2), and multiple pre-planned robustness checks (alpha=0.05 in Table 8, on-target subsets Table 9, GE0 Table 11, script partition Table 12, bottom-quintile floor Table 10, LID-threshold sweep Table 6, mGPT cross-reference §D.2). Evidence strength is high: headline claims (calibration-vs-detection failure distinction; distortion-free schemes most distorting; between-family disparity dominance) are backed by concrete numbers, e.g., Unigram-Gemma TPR 0.000 with AUC 0.986 recovered to 0.799 after recalibration (§5.1), between-family share median >90% (§5.1) and >=70% in 32/36 quality cells (§5.2), plus a mechanism-regression appendix with stated caveats. Generalizability is decent but bounded: framework transfers to other schemes/languages, yet only 6 schemes and 11 languages with six singleton families limit the typological decomposition's identifiability (§3, §6 Limitations). Reproducibility is mixed: models, datasets (FLORES++, AYA), generation parameters, thresholds, and compute (Appendix A) are specified, but no code or data release is stated.

primary_link.title: Auditing Cross-Lingual Fairness in Language Model Watermarking

papers.summary: Watermarking schemes for large language model output are evaluated almost exclusively on English text using each scheme's detection threshold and a narrow set of quality measurements. Multilingual deployment exposes evaluation-design choices that are inconsequential on English but determine conclusions cross-lingually. We propose an evaluation framework with four components: detection thresholds calibrated empirically per deployment context, a threshold-independent companion measurement that dis
papers.summary_zh: 文字浮水印旨在為 LLM 輸出嵌入可偵測的統計特徵,但現有方案幾乎只在英文上評估,且沿用各方案預設閾值與單一品質指標。本文提出首個跨語言公平性稽核框架,包含四個構件:依部署情境經驗校準偵測閾值、與閾值無關的 AUC 伴隨指標以區分校準失敗與偵測失敗、三種互不重疊的品質評量(MAUVE、BERTScore、參考模型困惑度),以及對類型學分族的廣義熵分解。實驗涵蓋 6 種浮水印方案、3 個開源生成器、11 種語言(橫跨 4 種文字與 8 個語系)及 base 與 instruct 兩種生成情境,產生約 20 萬組對照生成。關鍵發現:Unigram-Gemma 與 XSIR-Qwen 在全域閾值下看似偵測全失效,實為校準失敗,按語言重新校準即大幅回升;instruct 情境普遍壓縮偵測能力;理論上無失真的 SynthID 與 EXPEdit 實測反而失真最重;且跨語言差異多集中於語系層級(中位數超過 90%),顯示不公正是結構性而非個別語言特異。作者承認語言與方案覆蓋有限。此研究凸顯現行浮水印對部分語系使用者的保護力較弱、品質代價分配不均,需在 tokenizer 建構與分區設計等架構層面重新思考。
papers.title: Auditing Cross-Lingual Fairness in Language Model Watermarking
papers.title_zh: 稽核語言模型浮水印的跨語言公平性

links.title: Repo0: Design-Driven Zero-to-All Code Generation

evidence: Abstract + Table II: 'improves Functionality Coverage by up to 20.08 percentage points and Pass Rate by up to 29.74' verified: django GPT-5 mini Cov 80.50 vs RPG 60.42 (+20.08); statsmodels DeepSeek Pass 69.03 vs 39.29 (+29.74).
Section III-E: 'the main experiment reports three representative RepoCraft repositories: requests, statsmodels, and django'; remaining three repos and prompts deferred to supplementary.pdf on GitHub.

Section III-E: thresholds gamma_split=2/3, theta_merge=0.7 chosen on two held-out Commit0 Lite repos (wcwidth, sphinx) by 'manually comparing the evolved architectures with the corresponding ground-truth repository architectures' — subjective, partially reproducible tuning.

Table III vs Table II inconsistency: Repo0 on django shows Cov 80.50/Vot 97.12 (Table II) but Cov 87.50/Vot 100.00 (Table III) while Nov 13.59 and Pass 74.36 match, indicating unexplained result variance or error.

Section IV-C RQ3: metrics-guided convergence outperforms w/o evolution and budgeted LLM-decided variants on statsmodels (Cov 75.90->80.68, Pass 81.90->85.51), supporting the explicit convergence-criterion claim with a controlled comparison.
Section VI External Validity: experiments 'remain limited to a single programming language and benchmark' (six Python repositories from RepoCraft).

Footnote 1: 'Our code and data are available at https://github.com/cslsolow/Repo0'; Section III-D uses cross-model evaluation (DeepSeek judges GPT-5 mini outputs and vice versa) 'to mitigate evaluator bias', with three independent runs averaged (Section III-E).
llm_evaluation.rationale: In-scope LLM-agent methodology paper on repository-level code generation using GPT-5 mini and DeepSeek V3.2, squarely matching the highest-weight preferences (LLMs, agents, code). The core contribution—treating repository architecture as a continuously evolving Dual-DAG state driven by cohesion/coupling metrics until structural convergence, rather than a static one-shot plan (RPG)—is a genuine but incremental novelty. Rigor is solid: three RQs, two backbones, three baselines, four-component ablations, a controlled RQ3 comparison against budgeted LLM-decided evolution, three averaged runs, and a threats-to-validity section. Evidence is weakened by reporting only 3 of 6 RepoCraft repositories in the main table, an internal inconsistency (django GPT-5 mini Repo0: Cov 80.50/Vot 97.12 in Table II vs Cov 87.50/Vot 100.00 in Table III), LLM-based evaluation metrics, no significance testing or variance, and subjective manual threshold tuning against golden architectures on held-out repos. Headline gains (up to +20.08 Cov, +29.74 Pass vs RPG) are arithmetically consistent with Table II. Generalizability is limited to Python and a single benchmark, acknowledged in Section VI. Code, data, and prompts are claimed public, aiding reproducibility, though the manual threshold-selection step is hard to replicate exactly.

primary_link.title: Repo0: Design-Driven Zero-to-All Code Generation

papers.summary: Large language model agents have made substantial progress in code generation, yet most existing systems assume a predefined repository architecture. This assumption does not hold in zero-to-all code generation, where an agent must construct an entire software project directly from natural-language requirements while maintaining a modular repository architecture throughout development. We present Repo0, a continuous structural evolution framework for zero-to-all code generation. Repo0 maintains
papers.summary_zh: 現有程式碼生成代理多半假設儲存庫架構已事先設計好,但在 zero-to-all 情境下,代理必須僅憑自然語言需求從零建構整個軟體專案,並全程維持模組化架構。本文提出 Repo0,將儲存庫生成視為連續的結構演化問題:系統維護一個 Dual-DAG 架構狀態,包含需求層級 DAG、元件層級 DAG 及兩者的對齊關係,並透過 add、split、merge、revise、save 等結構動作,依內聚與耦合指標反覆調整元件邊界,待結構收斂後再以測試驅動開發(TDD)產生程式碼。作者在 RepoCraft 的六個真實 Python 儲存庫上,以 GPT-5 mini 與 DeepSeek V3.2 進行評估:Repo0 在所有設定皆取得最高功能覆蓋率與通過率,相較最強基線 RPG,功能覆蓋率最多提升 20.08 個百分點、通過率最多提升 29.74 個百分點。消融實驗顯示結構演化貢獻最大,且指標引導的收斂優於讓 LLM 自行決定結構動作,後者容易過度拆解架構而損害正確性。限制包括僅涵蓋 Python 與單一基準,結構更新品質亦依賴骨幹模型能力。此研究的意義在於指出儲存庫生成不只是寫碼,更需要顯式的架構推理與持續的結構精煉,為長期軟體工程代理指出新方向。
papers.title: Repo0: Design-Driven Zero-to-All Code Generation
papers.title_zh: Repo0:設計驅動的 Zero-to-All 程式碼生成
